title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Splat2Act: Personalized VLA Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
The authors introduce Splat2Act, a real‑to‑sim‑to‑real pipeline that builds building‑scale digital twins from a handheld phone scan using 3D Gaussian splatting, automatically discovers receptacles, and generates thousands of simulated pickup demonstrations to fine‑tune a pretrained vision‑language‑action policy. On a real Stretch‑3 robot the personalized policy reaches about 64% success on a 12‑task subset, showing that simulation‑oracle data can bridge the gap to real deployments.

### The Caveats
The real‑world evaluation is limited to a 12‑task pickup subset, so broader scene‑scale personalization has not been demonstrated.

## BT-Agent: Onboard LLM Robot Agents

### The Breakthrough
BT‑Agent blends large‑language‑model reasoning with behavior‑tree execution, enabling a 9 B model to run fully onboard a quadruped and abort unsafe actions locally. A new multi‑fidelity benchmark (text‑only throughput 10.9× higher, plus Habitat simulation) shows gains of about 10 pp at 4 B parameters and 5 pp at 9 B over the strongest Act/ReAct baseline.

### The Caveats
Improvements rely mostly on text‑only evaluation of 161 tasks, with only 39 runs in Habitat and no broader hardware tests beyond a single quadruped.

## Chronos Policy: Time‑Aware Control

### The Breakthrough
Chronos Policy makes physical time explicit in a diffusion transformer via timestamp embeddings or a novel time‑aware RoPE, and trains with temporally randomized data so the policy can handle asynchronous, multi‑rate sensors. Experiments on simulated and real robots report robustness gains on dynamic and multisensory tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper provides performance gains but no comparison to established baselines, leaving superiority uncertain.

## Noise Space Learning for VLA Adaptation

### The Breakthrough
Noise Space Learning keeps a pretrained vision‑language‑action model frozen and learns a context‑conditioned noise distribution to steer it during reinforcement learning, integrating with PPO, SAC, and AWR. Evaluations on the LIBERO benchmark, RoboTwin simulator, and four real‑robot manipulation tasks show competitive performance under tight compute and interaction budgets.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparisons are reported, so improvement over existing VLA adaptation methods is unclear.

## Quattro ZBD ESP32 Quadruped Firmware

### The Breakthrough
The open‑source firmware runs a 12‑DOF quadruped on an ESP32 using a dual‑core FreeRTOS design: core 1 executes 120 Hz inverse‑kinematics while core 0 handles Wi‑Fi, UDP control, UI and optional Bluetooth, with Kalman‑filtered IMU leveling and programmable emotes, enabling a low‑cost fully embedded walking robot.

### The Caveats
Capabilities are described qualitatively; no quantitative performance data, robustness testing, or comparisons to other controllers are provided.

## nano-ros: no_std Rust ROS2 Client

### The Breakthrough
nano‑ros implements a full ROS 2 client in Rust without the standard library, supporting multiple back‑ends (Zenoh, XRCE‑DDS, CycloneDDS) and running on bare‑metal MCUs and RTOS kernels (Zephyr, FreeRTOS, NuttX, ThreadX) with formal verification tooling for safety‑critical analysis.

### The Caveats
Validation is limited to QEMU emulation; no real‑hardware benchmarks or performance data are shown.

## PyPose: Differentiable Lie‑Group Library

### The Breakthrough
PyPose introduces a LieTensor abstraction for batched SO(3), SE(3), Sim(3) etc., with automatic differentiation, and provides EKF, UKF, LQR, and Gauss‑Newton/Levenberg‑Marquardt optimizers that outperform the Theseus library in speed and memory on GPU‑accelerated batched kernels.

### The Caveats
Benchmarks focus on simulated kernel performance against a single baseline, without end‑to‑end robot task validation.

## agentenv-framework SDK

### The Breakthrough
Scale AI’s agentenv‑framework packages RL environments as Docker images that communicate via an open protocol, offering versioned, reproducible benchmarks with a CLI for local or cloud deployment, easing the creation of realistic simulation worlds for embodied‑AI research.

### The Caveats
The framework is released without any hardware or benchmark validation, so its applicability to real‑world robot tasks remains unproven.

## Meta Muse Wonder Models

### The Breakthrough
Meta unveils Muse Wonder models that add Active Memory for long‑term context retention and Active Focus for iterative problem solving, combining large‑scale pretraining with reinforcement learning to achieve top‑line results on legal, focus, and coding benchmarks.

### The Caveats
State‑of‑the‑art performance is unsupported—no baseline models are named and results are confined to software benchmarks with no real‑world or robotic validation.

### Priority
Splat2Act is the most actionable story because it demonstrates a complete, end‑to‑end simulation‑to‑real pipeline that already works on a physical robot, offering a concrete template for rapid scene‑specific manipulation.

### One action
Reproduce the Splat2Act pipeline on your own tabletop scene using a phone scan and a compatible VLA policy to assess feasibility for your robot.

### What to watch
Several papers target vision‑language‑action manipulation: Splat2Act shows a full sim‑to‑real pipeline with scene‑specific fine‑tuning; Noise Space Learning proposes a lightweight noise‑based adaptation that keeps the base model frozen; BT‑Agent integrates LLM reasoning with behavior‑trees for onboard decision making. Watching how these approaches compare on broader task suites and real‑robot deployments will indicate which strategy scales best for embodied AI.
